tabimorelin.summary: An experimental oral growth hormone secretagogue that people discuss as a route to higher GH for a leaner, more muscular body.

quick.overview:
Tabimorelin is an experimental oral drug from the first generation of growth hormone secretagogues. People who discuss it are after the body-composition payoff of higher growth hormone: a leaner, more muscular look.

It mimics ghrelin at the GH secretagogue receptor, which triggers growth hormone release. It was tested in healthy men and in adults with growth hormone deficiency, where it raised growth hormone and IGF-1. Those studies measured hormone release, and none measured appearance or body composition.
quick.how: It was never marketed, so there is no established routine. In peptide and bodybuilding circles it is grouped with other GH secretagogues as an oral option, usually discussed as part of a broader body-composition plan alongside training and diet.
quick.risks: It inhibits the liver enzyme CYP3A4, so interactions with other drugs are possible. Human data come from a few early studies, and it was never approved for any use.

angle.text: Tabimorelin is discussed as an oral way to raise growth hormone, with the aim of a leaner, more muscular body. It stimulates GH release through the ghrelin receptor, and a few early human trials measured that hormone response.

ghrp-1.summary: An early growth hormone releasing peptide that bodybuilding communities group with GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 to raise GH for muscle and fat loss.

quick.overview:
GHRP-1 is one of the first synthetic growth hormone releasing peptides, developed alongside GHRP-6 and GHRP-2. People look to it for higher growth hormone, which they connect to more muscle and less body fat.

It binds the ghrelin/GH secretagogue receptor, separate from the GHRH receptor, and prompts growth hormone release. A 1993 review reported that it, GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 were the three such peptides given to humans, and that all released more GH than GHRH 1-44. Studies measured hormone release; body-composition outcomes have not been tested.
quick.how: It is discussed in peptide and bodybuilding communities as one of the older GHRPs, usually in the context of a muscle-building or fat-loss plan. It was largely superseded by later peptides.
quick.risks: It is a research peptide, not an approved medicine, and little modern human safety data exists. It is prohibited in sport, and anti-doping labs have developed urine tests for it and its metabolites.

angle.text: GHRP-1 is grouped with GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 as a way to raise growth hormone for muscle gain and fat loss. It stimulates GH release through the ghrelin receptor, and some 1990s human work measured that release.

alexamorelin.summary: A hexarelin-related GH secretagogue peptide that appears in growth hormone lists for muscle and fat loss, and is mostly known from anti-doping screening.

quick.overview:
Alexamorelin is a lab-made peptide related to hexarelin that stimulates growth hormone release. The draw is more growth hormone, which people link to muscle gain and fat loss.

As a growth hormone secretagogue, it is described as raising the body's own GH output rather than supplying GH itself. A 2000 study reported its endocrine effects in humans. It appears in the literature mainly as one of the peptides that anti-doping laboratories screen for; no study has tested it for muscle or appearance outcomes.
quick.how: It is rare and obscure, appearing mostly in lists of GH secretagogues. There is no established routine for it.
quick.risks: No clinical-trial safety data were found. It is not an approved drug and is covered by sports drug-testing screens.

angle.text: Alexamorelin is a hexarelin-related peptide listed among growth hormone secretagogues, where the appeal is more GH for muscle and fat loss. A 2000 study reported its hormonal effects in humans.

deslorelin.summary: A veterinary GnRH-agonist implant that shifts sex-hormone output; it appears on hormone lists for its effect on puberty-linked growth and looks.

quick.overview:
Deslorelin is a lab-made GnRH agonist mostly sold for animals, such as implants that suppress fertility in dogs and ferrets or trigger ovulation in horses. It shows up on hormone-focused lists because GnRH agonists change LH and sex-hormone output, which in turn shapes puberty-linked growth and looks.

It acts on the pituitary GnRH receptor; continuous exposure suppresses reproductive hormones after an initial surge. In humans it has been studied in research settings, including long-term treatment of children with precocious puberty. No studies address appearance or muscle use.
quick.how: Its use is veterinary, as a slow-release implant. In hormone-focused discussions it is mentioned as one of several GnRH agonists, with related drugs used in pediatric endocrinology.
quick.risks: It is not approved for general human use. Human safety data come from specialist trials in children and patients, and the veterinary product Ovuplant was withdrawn in the US after fertility-timing problems in mares.

angle.text: Deslorelin is a GnRH agonist that changes LH and sex-hormone output, which is why it appears on hormone lists tied to puberty-linked growth and looks. Pediatric endocrine research exists on related drugs.

ganirelix.summary: A GnRH-antagonist IVF drug that quickly suppresses LH and FSH, which is why it comes up in hormone-manipulation talk in physique circles.

quick.overview:
Ganirelix is a prescription injection used during IVF to stop the body ovulating too early. In muscle and physique circles it is mentioned because it rapidly lowers LH and FSH, and with them sex-hormone levels.

It blocks GnRH receptors on the pituitary, and the effect reverses after stopping. Randomized trials in women undergoing ovarian stimulation compared it with GnRH agonist protocols. All the clinical research comes from fertility treatment; no study tests it for appearance or muscle goals.
quick.how: Clinically it is used for a short window during ovarian stimulation in IVF cycles. Its appearance use in physique forums is theoretical.
quick.risks: Reported effects include injection-site reactions, abdominal pain, headache and nausea. It is not for use in pregnancy and is prescription-only.

angle.text: Ganirelix is an IVF drug that blocks pituitary GnRH receptors and quickly suppresses LH and FSH, so it is mentioned in hormone-manipulation discussions in physique circles. The clinical research comes from fertility treatment.

humanin.summary: A mitochondria-derived peptide studied in cells and animals for cell protection, promoted in longevity circles as a way to stay youthful-looking.

quick.overview:
Humanin is a small peptide made from mitochondrial DNA, discovered in 2001 during Alzheimer research. In longevity circles it is promoted as a way to slow aging, which people connect to staying youthful-looking.

It is reported to block apoptosis by interfering with Bax and to act on cell-surface receptors including formyl peptide receptors. Laboratory and animal work links it to cell protection, insulin action and inflammation. Studies are in cells, animals and observational human work; no human trials have tested it as a treatment, and none looked at skin or visible aging.
quick.how: It is a research peptide discussed in longevity communities, with no established human routine.
quick.risks: No human safety data from treatment trials were found. Some research reports it may impair chemotherapy and promote tumor growth in cancer models. It is not an approved drug.

angle.text: Humanin is promoted as a mitochondrial peptide that protects cells and could slow aging, which people tie to looking younger for longer. The research so far is in cells and animals.

dihexa.summary: An experimental angiotensin IV-derived peptide that nootropic users take for memory and learning, studied in rodents.

quick.overview:
Dihexa is a lab-made peptide derived from angiotensin IV, designed to resist breakdown and cross the blood-brain barrier. Nootropic users take it for memory and learning, which they tie to study and work performance rather than to looks.

It is reported to bind hepatocyte growth factor and boost signalling through the c-Met receptor, promoting synapse formation in cell cultures. It has been studied in rodents for memory impairment, and a 2021 study reported it rescued cognitive impairment in an Alzheimer mouse model, linked to the PI3K/AKT pathway. No human trial has been published.
quick.how: It is sold as a research chemical and discussed in nootropic communities. There is no established human routine.
quick.risks: Human safety is unknown. Authors have raised the theoretical concern that sustained c-Met activation could promote tumors. It is not an approved drug.

angle.text: Dihexa is taken by nootropic users for sharper memory and focus, which they connect to study and work performance. It has been studied in rodents for memory, and no human trials exist.

selank.summary: A Russian-developed anxiolytic peptide that forum users take for calmer social situations and better focus, supporting a more confident presence.

quick.overview:
Selank is a synthetic seven-amino-acid peptide derived from tuftsin, developed in Russia and registered there as nasal drops for anxiety. Forum users group it with Semax and Cerebrolysin as a nootropic, taking it for calmer social situations and focus, which they connect to a more relaxed, confident presence.

Studies in cells and animals suggest it may influence GABA-related gene expression and inhibit enkephalin-degrading enzymes, which researchers propose as routes to its anxiolytic effects. Human evidence is a handful of Russian-language studies on anxiety. No published trial has examined appearance outcomes.
quick.how: It is used as nasal drops in Russia. Elsewhere users discuss it as a nootropic, often alongside Semax.
quick.risks: It is a registered drug only in Russia; outside Russia it is sold as a research chemical without regulatory oversight. A 2021 pharmacology review grouped it among agents acting on GABA receptors.

angle.text: Selank is taken for a calmer anxiety response and easier social situations, which users connect to a more relaxed, confident presence. Human evidence is a handful of Russian-language studies on anxiety.

cerebrolysin.summary: A porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved for stroke and dementia in many countries, used by forum members as an iqmaxxing nootropic for study performance.

quick.overview:
Cerebrolysin is an injectable mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and amino acids prepared from porcine brain protein. It is approved in many countries for stroke, traumatic brain injury and dementia. In forum threads on iqmaxxing and brainmaxxing, members use it hoping for sharper studying and exam performance.

Preclinical studies report it mimics neurotrophic factor activity and promotes neurogenesis in rodent stroke and Alzheimer models, including through the Sonic hedgehog pathway. Human trials are in neurological patients, including the CARS trial in post-stroke recovery and a meta-analysis of nine randomized trials. Its effect in healthy people has not been studied, and one small registered study listed hair repigmentation during therapy.
quick.how: Clinically it is given by injection or infusion in courses under medical supervision. Forum members discuss it as a nootropic stack addition.
quick.risks: It is an animal-derived injectable and a prescription product where approved. Members mention obtaining it from unofficial sources, which carries quality and sterility concerns.

angle.text: Cerebrolysin is discussed as an iqmaxxing nootropic for sharper study performance, building on trials in stroke and dementia. It is not an appearance compound.

noopept-omberacetam.summary: A Russian-developed racetam-like nootropic that people take for memory, focus and mood, with small human studies on cognition.

quick.overview:
Noopept is a synthetic nootropic developed in Russia, related to the racetams, and sold online as a supplement in many countries. People take it for memory, focus and mood, and in appearance forums it appears in stacks aimed at productivity.

Laboratory studies suggest antioxidant effects, reduced excitotoxicity and raised growth factors such as BDNF in rodents. It is described as a prodrug of the dipeptide cycloprolylglycine. Human evidence is a small number of Russian clinical comparisons with piracetam; no appearance outcome has been tested.
quick.how: It is taken as a supplement, usually alone or as part of a nootropic stack, for study and work sessions.
quick.risks: Long-term human safety studies have not been published. It is an unapproved new drug in the US, prescription-only in Australia and registered as a medicine in Russia.

angle.text: Noopept is taken as a nootropic for memory, focus and mood, aimed at better study and work output. Small human studies exist for cognition.

coluracetam.summary: A racetam developed for Alzheimer's and depression and later sold online as a nootropic for focus and mood.

quick.overview:
Coluracetam is an experimental racetam developed by Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma, first for Alzheimer's and later licensed for depression and anxiety. It is now sold online as a nootropic that people take for focus and mood.

It enhances high-affinity choline uptake in rodent brain tissue, a step in acetylcholine synthesis; AMPA-related effects have also been suggested. Its research base is those pharma programs, and it has no appearance angle.
quick.how: It is sold as a nootropic supplement and discussed in racetam stacks for mental performance.
quick.risks: It has never been approved and development was discontinued. Side-effect data are limited, and it is prescription-only in Australia.

angle.text: Coluracetam is a racetam taken as a nootropic for focus and mood, drawing on its development for Alzheimer's and depression. It is used for mental performance.

fasoracetam.summary: A never-marketed racetam studied for ADHD that nootropic users take for focus and attention.

quick.overview:
Fasoracetam is a racetam discovered by Nippon Shinyaku in the late 1980s. It was tested for vascular dementia, then repurposed for ADHD and a genetic syndrome, and is now sold online as a nootropic that users take for focus and attention.

It appears to modulate metabotropic glutamate receptors. Human research is limited to small trials. Its role in the nootropic stack is mental performance.
quick.how: It is taken as a nootropic supplement, typically in racetam-style stacks for study and work.
quick.risks: It is not approved for any use. Side-effect information is limited to small trials.

angle.text: Fasoracetam is a racetam that nootropic users take for focus and attention, following its trials in ADHD. It sits in the nootropic stack for better mental performance.

nefiracetam.summary: A Japanese racetam studied for dementia and post-stroke apathy that nootropic users take for memory and drive.

quick.overview:
Nefiracetam is an oral racetam-class nootropic studied mainly in Japan for dementia and apathy after stroke. Nootropic users take it for memory and drive.

Lab studies point to effects on calcium channels, acetylcholine receptors and the GABA system. It is sold online as a supplement.
quick.how: It is taken orally as a nootropic, often discussed alongside other racetams for study and motivation.
quick.risks: It is not approved in most countries; it is unscheduled in the US and prescription-only in Australia. Animal toxicity (kidney, testis) was seen in dogs, while human trials reported none.

angle.text: Nefiracetam is a Japanese racetam studied for dementia and post-stroke apathy, and nootropic users take it for memory and drive. It is used for mental performance.

sunifiram.summary: An experimental nootropic that users take for learning and focus, based on animal studies of antiamnesic effects.

quick.overview:
Sunifiram is an experimental nootropic from a series of piperazine compounds made by Italian researchers, a simplified analogue of unifiram. Users take it for learning and focus, aiming at better study performance.

In animal studies it showed antiamnesic effects at much lower doses than piracetam. Its mechanism is unknown; research points to NMDA glycine-site and kinase pathways. There are no human trials.
quick.how: It is sold online and discussed in nootropic communities as a potent option for study sessions.
quick.risks: As of 2016 it had undergone no toxicology testing and no human trials. It is unapproved anywhere, including the US.

angle.text: Sunifiram is taken by nootropic users for learning and focus, based on animal studies showing strong antiamnesic effects. There are no human trials.

unifiram.summary: The parent compound of sunifiram, sold online as a potent nootropic for memory and focus; research is in animals.

quick.overview:
Unifiram is an experimental nootropic from Italian labs and the parent of sunifiram. It is sold online for memory and focus.

In animal studies it showed antiamnesic effects with far greater potency than piracetam. Its mechanism is unknown; indirect AMPA pathway involvement has been suggested. Evidence is limited to animal work.
quick.how: It is discussed in nootropic communities as a potent compound for study and focus, and is sold online.
quick.risks: No human or long-term toxicity studies exist. It is unapproved and not patented.

angle.text: Unifiram is sold as a potent nootropic for memory and focus, aimed at better study performance. Research is limited to animal studies.

modafinil.summary: A prescription wakefulness drug that forum users take to stay alert and productive; some report feeling more sociable.

quick.overview:
Modafinil is an FDA-approved prescription drug for excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work disorder. In looksmaxxing and self-improvement forums people take it to stay alert and study and work longer, which supports a steadier routine. Some also report feeling more sociable or charismatic.

The label says the mechanism is unknown, and a 2009 imaging study in healthy men found it binds the dopamine transporter and raises dopamine. Posters link it to looks indirectly, for example through appetite suppression. No trial has tested it for appearance, and evidence on cognitive effects in healthy people is mixed.
quick.how: Users take it by mouth in the morning as a daily or occasional aid for focused work or study. Some combine it with other nootropics.
quick.risks: The label warns of serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity reactions, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events. Users report headache and reduced appetite. It is prescription-only in the US.

angle.text: Users take modafinil to stay alert and work or study longer, which feeds a steadier routine, and some report feeling more sociable. It is approved for sleepiness in narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work.

armodafinil.summary: The longer-acting R-enantiomer of modafinil, prescribed for sleepiness and used by forum members the same way for alertness.

quick.overview:
Armodafinil is the R-enantiomer of modafinil, approved in the US for excessive sleepiness in narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work disorder. In looksmaxxing forums it comes up as an alternative to modafinil for staying alert and productive, supporting a steadier routine.

The label says the mechanism is unknown and similar to modafinil. Research reports it inhibits dopamine reuptake at the dopamine transporter, and a 2012 study found properties that may differ from the racemic mixture. No trial has tested it for appearance.
quick.how: It is taken orally, usually in the morning, in the same way as modafinil, as a daily or occasional aid for study and work.
quick.risks: The label warns of serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events. It is prescription-only in the US.

angle.text: Armodafinil is the longer-acting form of modafinil, used for alertness and productivity, which supports a steadier routine. It is prescribed for sleepiness in narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work.

adrafinil.summary: A modafinil prodrug once sold in France for vigilance in older adults, used as an over-the-counter route to the same alertness.

quick.overview:
Adrafinil is converted by the liver into modafinil, so users take it as a non-prescription route to the same wakefulness for study and work. It was sold in France as Olmifon from the mid-1980s for sleepiness and inattention in older adults until 2011.

Its effects are attributed to modafinil, which acts on the dopamine transporter. Human clinical research is thin, and no trial has tested it for appearance outcomes.
quick.how: It is sold as a supplement or research chemical in some markets and taken orally for alertness and productivity.
quick.risks: Human safety data are limited. It is not approved for any use in the US and is listed as a stimulant in doping control.

angle.text: Adrafinil is turned into modafinil in the body, so users take it for alertness and a steadier work and study routine without a prescription. It was sold in France for vigilance in older adults.

citicoline-cdp-choline.summary: A choline-donor nootropic used for focus and memory, studied for stroke and brain injury.

quick.overview:
Citicoline is a naturally occurring nucleotide that supplies choline and cytidine for membrane synthesis. It is sold as a supplement in the US and used as a drug in some countries for stroke and cognitive decline. People take it as a nootropic for focus and memory.

After ingestion it is broken down into choline and cytidine, which the brain uses to make phosphatidylcholine, a membrane phospholipid. Pooled analyses of earlier trials suggested benefit in stroke, while the large ICTUS and COBRIT trials did not show overall benefit in stroke or brain injury. No trial tests it for appearance.
quick.how: It is taken orally as a supplement, usually as part of a nootropic or brain-health routine.
quick.risks: Grokipedia describes a good safety profile at therapeutic amounts.

angle.text: Citicoline supplies choline for brain cell membranes and is taken as a nootropic for focus and memory, aimed at better mental performance. It has been studied for stroke and brain injury.

alpha-gpc.summary: A choline donor sold as a cognitive and sports supplement that lifters use for focus and training output.

quick.overview:
Alpha-GPC is a choline-containing compound sold as a supplement, and as a prescription drug for cognitive decline in Italy. Lifters take it for focus and training output, hoping for harder sessions that support muscle gain.

It supplies choline, a precursor of acetylcholine and of membrane phospholipids, and rat studies reported raised hippocampal acetylcholine. Most human research is older Italian multicentre work in stroke, transient ischaemic attacks and dementia, with newer registered trials in cognition and athletic performance in healthy adults. One 2024 trial lists growth hormone as an outcome. No study has tested appearance outcomes.
quick.how: It is taken orally as a supplement, commonly before training or as part of a nootropic routine.
quick.risks: Older Italian trials reported low adverse event rates; detailed safety data are limited. It is sold as a supplement in the US and is not FDA-approved as a drug.

angle.text: Alpha-GPC is a choline source that lifters take for focus and training output, aiming at harder sessions that support muscle gain. It is a prescription drug for cognitive decline in Italy.
